Nurton, h., in Pattingham, 54 m. W. of Wolverhampton. 13 c. Noverton. ‘Noverton’ has puzzled me exceedingly. After concluding that it was untranslatable, it suddenly occurred to me that the initial # was excrescent, and that the original form was Overton, upper town (A. S. Ofertine), and the difficulty vanished. An excrescent initial z arises generally from the use of a word in the dative form, commencing with a vowel, e.g. a/len oke (at the oak) becomes a/fe noke, hence our family name Noake; atten ash becomes Nash; an ewt becomes a newt; mine uncle my nuncle, &c.
